title: What Happens to Your EV at 20°F? ❄️🔋 #shorts

scenes.text: What happens to your EV at twenty degrees Fahrenheit? In a triple A lab test, range fell forty one percent.
First, cold thickens the battery's electrolyte, so lithium ions move slower.
Second, heat. A gas engine's waste heat warms you for free. An EV pays from its battery.
A basic heater is like a toaster: one unit of electricity, one unit of heat.
A heat pump moves heat in from outside, giving more heat than the power it uses.
Across over eighteen thousand EVs, cars with heat pumps kept about eighty three percent of range in freezing weather. Without, about seventy five.
Tip: warm it up while plugged in. Would winter change which EV you buy? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
